newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs edge up in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs edge up in listless trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures inched up on Wednesday but dealers said activity was in tight ranges and low volumes amid a dearth of new leads.
"The Bank of Japan bought 100 billion yen worth of bonds in the morning. But there's not been much news after that, and no major players in the market either," a trader at a U.S. futures house said.
She said the bond buying operation was supportive of the market but some of the gains were erased by players taking profit.
December Euroyen stood at 98.85 at 1110 GMT against its IMM close at 98.83 on volume of 10,310 lots.
The new benchmark September JGB contract ended at 122.72 against its opening 122.45.
"At the current level, December Euroyen has probably priced in a fair amount of risk for rates to go up before the year end," a European bank dealer said.
He said December Euroyen should remain within a broad range of 98.70-99.00.
Eurodollar futures had an even more uninspired session, ending scarcely changed on very low turnover.

Dealers said the market lacked clear direction due to varying signals in U.S. economic data and there was no clear consensus on whether the Federal Reserve would hike short-term U.S. rates at its next meeting in July.
"Broadly, the Eurodollars could be on an uptrend. But this is a pretty expensive level," the bank dealer said.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.790 against their IMM close at 93.795 on volume of 4,425 lots.
